differences.what: massing: a long, low, single-storey house on the north bank, its ridge along the river and a gable at each end, the west gable toward the eye; the build's two ends land on the drawn ones (x 108 and 310 px) within about 10 px on the red-edge overlay
walls: drawn dark, hatched in horizontal courses, as hewn log reads; the build's are squared log (Moses and Kirkland)
piazza: across the whole front on posts with a rail between them, five posts visible east of the west gable (x 213-305 px); the build's six-post piazza puts five there, within about 13 px

stacks: Lossing draws two through the ridge, at x 200 px (0.4 of the ridge from the west gable) and x 163 px (by the west gable). The build's middle stack lands at x 194 px on his x 200; its other stands by the EAST gable (x 242 px), where the 1857 engraving, the Teich postcard and the Cram plate put the second stack. Where they disagree, the 1857 engraving governs: it is twelve years earlier, made in Chicago, and draws the roof plainly; Lossing drew the house from a distance, more than fifty years after the fort burned

a dark mass behind the roof east of the stacks (x 240-280 px, y 250-270 px): it may be the far slope in shadow or a building behind. The 1857 engraving shows no range behind the house, so none is built; Wau-Bun's outbuildings and Ouilmette's and Pettell's cabins behind the house are T-2484's other pieces
openings: the front is in the piazza's shadow and no door or window is legible

the paling across the front from beyond the west gable, the four poplars in a row receding east, and the great tree behind the house's west end: built outside this GLB, as kinzie_house_1812_green (its west side 13.4 m beyond the west gable, as drawn) and data/flora/plantings/kinzie_house_1812_trees.json; this render is the house alone

piazza roof: Lossing carries the main roof down over the piazza in one plane, its eave at y 293 px. Rebuilt (T-2516) as the main roof carried down over the piazza, broken to a flatter pitch above the front wall: Sarony and Eastman draw that break close to, and it is the one roof that answers all five pictures. From this low eye the break shows where Lossing draws none

piazza height: Lossing's posts are about 32 px tall and the rebuilt ones (Sarony's 2.95 m plate) draw about 39 px, every head about 7 px above the drawn head; T-2497's 2.0 m posts matched him. Sarony's lithograph governs; Lossing drew the house from a distance more than fifty years after the fort burned
the west end: drawn dark and hatched, in shade, with no opening legible; the light, window and door Sarony draws on it are built

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
